thread.title_full: Eaton County warns residents about scam emails impersonating planning and zoning department

author: Capitol News
title: Eaton County warns residents about scam emails impersonating planning and zoning department
text:
Jim Mott, Chairman | Eaton County
Jim Mott, Chairman | Eaton County
Eaton County officials have warned residents about a recent wave of scam emails targeting individuals who have interacted with the county's Planning & Zoning Department. The fraudulent messages often mention permits, zoning applications, or payments and are intended to obtain personal or financial information from recipients. In several instances, scammers have asked residents to wire transfer money directly.
Authorities noted that even those who have not engaged with the Planning & Zoning Department could still receive these deceptive emails. Residents are advised not to reply, click on links, or open attachments in suspicious messages. They should mark such emails as spam or phishing and delete them. Officials also recommend checking that any legitimate communication comes from an email address ending in @eatoncounty.org without additional language.
The county cautions residents to be wary of urgent or threatening language and requests for payment to Eaton County made via email. Hovering over links before clicking can help reveal their true destination, and personal or financial information should never be shared by email.
Victims of these scams are encouraged to file a report with the Internet Crime Complaint Center at ic3.gov. According to officials, the FBI has automated capabilities through IC3 that may assist in recovering funds if reports are filed quickly and include detailed wire transfer information for both sender and recipient.
Residents who are uncertain about the authenticity of a message or wish to verify an invoice or application are urged to contact the relevant department directly or email [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection) for confirmation.
